// Parentheses are a node in the syntax tree, not whitespace. Every
// classification in this package type-asserts on the expression it is handed,
// so one pair of them around a checker was the difference between a violation
// and a clean gate, with nothing in the source to show which one it was.
package fixture

import (
	"testing"

	qt "github.com/frankban/quicktest"
)

// stepper has nothing to do with quicktest. Its Run is written with the same
// parentheses below and is not a violation.
type stepper struct{}

func (stepper) Run(name string, step func(int)) {}

// callbacks holds a subtest callback in a form this package cannot resolve
// without types, so the two rows that use it can only be reported through their
// receiver.
var callbacks = []func(*qt.C){func(c *qt.C) {}}

func TestParenthesizedReceiverBoundToAName(t *testing.T) {
	c := qt.New(t)

	run := (c).Run
	run("the method value is the same subtest", func(c *qt.C) {
		c.Assert(1, qt.Equals, 1)
	})
}

func TestParenthesizedReceiverCalled(t *testing.T) {
	c := qt.New(t)

	(c).Run("the parenthesized receiver is the same subtest", callbacks[0])
}

func TestParenthesizedAliasOfAChecker(t *testing.T) {
	c := qt.New(t)

	alias := (c)
	alias.Run("an alias written in parentheses is the same checker", callbacks[0])
}

func TestParenthesizedSubtestCallback(t *testing.T) {
	c := qt.New(t)

	t.Run("the borrowed checker is inside a parenthesized closure", (func(t *testing.T) {
		c.Assert(2, qt.Equals, 2)
	}))
}

// Two things a pair of parentheses must not turn into a violation: an unrelated
// runner, and a conforming subtest that writes its own parameter in them.
func TestParenthesesAreNotThemselvesAViolation(t *testing.T) {
	var steps stepper

	(steps).Run("an unrelated runner is not a subtest", func(int) {})

	t.Run("the closure builds from its own parameter", func(t *testing.T) {
		c := qt.New((t))
		c.Assert(3, qt.Equals, 3)
	})
}

// A type written in parentheses is the same type, and gofmt keeps them in a
// declaration. Neither of these has an initializer for the classification to
// fall back on, so the parentheses were the whole of it.
var held (*qt.C)

func TestParenthesizedCheckerType(t *testing.T) {
	held.Run("a checker declared with a parenthesized type is still a checker", callbacks[0])
}

func TestParenthesizedTBType(t *testing.T) {
	var parent (testing.TB)
	parent = t

	t.Run("the enclosing TB's type is parenthesized", func(t *testing.T) {
		parent.Log("work")
	})
}
